purpose: Source-status integration guidance only; no upstream files are patched.
article: From Polylogarithm Conjectures to Exact Reductions (9 October 2026)
article_paths: Relative to the deliverable archive; labels are the stable proof references.

status_definitions.proved: A locally supported candidate receives an explicit proof in this continuation.
status_definitions.known: A published result is identified or attributed; not counted as a newly solved conjecture.
status_definitions.inherited: Already proved in the previous project continuation and rederived here; excluded from the new count.
status_definitions.open: This continuation does not supply the requested proof/certificate; no global independence or literature-open claim is implied.

counting_cautions: The extra weight-five shuffle identity strengthens the spanning bound but is not another pre-existing candidate among the eleven.
The all-weight parity theorem, formal Lyndon quotient theorem and complementary-power family are general results/extensions, not extra candidate-count entries.
Formal quotient dimensions and numerical residuals are not proofs of numerical period independence.
The fixed-order moment expansion and cubic named Tornheim representation are known starting results; the late-coefficient and growing-truncation bounds are the new proved refinements.

entries.source_section: Candidate Gaussian reductions at weights five and six
entries.prior_status: Accepted numerical identity; the section explicitly withholds analytic status unless a derivation is supplied.
entries.proof_section: The weight-five relation is two shuffles
entries.evidence_summary: The exact row combination 960*(Li1 Li4 shuffle)-224*(Li2 Li3 shuffle) cancels pi^5 and reproduces every recorded coefficient. Retaining both rows gives a spanning set of at most two same-argument doubles modulo singles.
entries.integration_action: Promote the displayed relation to a proved identity and replace the at-most-three spanning claim by at-most-two; do not assert numerical independence.

entries.source_section: Hunting more ladder bases, and a methodological caveat; Ladders are Bloch-group elements
entries.source_display: First unlabelled trilogarithm row in the cubic/quartic pair
entries.prior_status: The raw formula is supported by two-engine and 400-digit checks. The corresponding P3 formula is called exact, but a local functional-equation certificate is not displayed.
entries.proof_section: Two Kummer substitutions prove the cubic trilogarithm
entries.evidence_summary: Two Kummer substitutions and one Landen equation give the exact P3 row certificate 4C+2B-48A. Four Rogers pentagons prove the dilogarithm tail identity; elementary factorizations remove the logarithmic corrections.
entries.integration_action: Supply the complete local proof and identify its classical functional-equation inputs. Do not claim a new general Kummer or Bloch-group theorem.

entries.source_section: Hunting more ladder bases, and a methodological caveat
entries.source_display: Second unlabelled trilogarithm row in the cubic/quartic pair
entries.prior_status: Displayed with two-engine and 400-digit numerical verification; no local functional-equation proof is supplied in this section.
entries.proof_section: A uniform ladder from a complementary pair of powers
entries.evidence_summary: Take (a,b)=(1,4) in the complementary-power Landen identity and multiply by -12. The Landen law has a complete real differentiation-and-endpoint proof.
entries.integration_action: Promote the row to a proved identity and present it as a specialization of the complementary-power family.

entries.item: Named Tornheim-derivative representation of M3 = integral_0^1 log(Gamma(x))^3 dx
entries.prior_status: The checkpoint calls finding the correct named depth-two atom open, while reporting a numerical value and unsuccessful single-value searches.
entries.proof_section: Log-gamma moments: correcting the open-problem boundary; A compact form of the cubic identity
entries.evidence_summary: Bailey, D. Borwein and J. M. Borwein, Theorem 6, already evaluated M3 using Tornheim derivatives. The present formula is an equivalent compact differential-operator form with an independent Fourier derivation.
entries.integration_action: Replace the broad named-atom open claim by a literature attribution. Reduction in a specified smaller algebra and numerical independence remain separate questions. The new 112-digit enclosure is a numerical certificate, not a new discovery of M3's named representation.

entries.source_display: No fixed-order asymptotic formula is printed here; the anchor identifies the related moment programme
entries.item: Known fixed-order factorial-moment expansion in exponential scales k^(-n)
entries.prior_status: The complete fixed-order large-n expansion is not displayed in this checkpoint section; it is already known from Amdeberhan et al., Theorem 8.1.
entries.status_scope: known starting theorem with new proved refinements; no new-conjecture credit
entries.proof_section: Log-gamma moments: correcting the open-problem boundary; Late coefficients and the inverse reciprocal gamma function; An effective remainder with a growing number of terms
entries.evidence_summary: Attribute the fixed-order expansion to Amdeberhan et al. The present extension proves c_k~C*rho^(-k)*k^(-3/2), divergence for every fixed n, and an explicit bound when K grows linearly with n.
entries.integration_action: Add the known expansion with its literature attribution and distinguish the proved late-coefficient and growing-truncation refinements. Never present the divergent infinite Dirichlet series as a convergent identity.

entries.source_section: Reshetnikov's conjectures, verified; Completing Tito's family: the unwritten weight-6 and weight-7 ladders; Two weights beyond: explicit ladders at weight 8 and 9; Canonical index-20/24 ladders and a zeta-elimination chain

entries.item: Complete local functional-equation certificates for the recorded golden ladders at weights 5 through 9
entries.prior_status: The checkpoint records high-precision verification and connections to Abouzahra--Lewin ladders; it does not display all local derivations for the recorded coefficient formulas.
entries.status_scope: open local certificate task; not a global literature-novelty claim
entries.proof_section: What the certificate establishes and what remains open
entries.evidence_summary: The present contribution proves the cubic and quartic weight-three identities and their complementary-power family. It does not establish the higher golden ladder formulas by pseudointegration or by an unproved higher Bloch-group assertion.
entries.integration_action: Do not upgrade these formulas on the strength of the new cubic/quartic proofs. Preserve any valid classical provenance and keep the missing local certificates as future work; this register does not claim that every higher golden identity is open in the published literature.
